page: Amazon Web Services m8g.medium is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AWS Graviton processor. Built on the ARMv9 architecture, it features a single dedicated physical core running an AWS Neoverse-V2 CPU at 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests place the processor in the average tier, supported by strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression performance. However, because the instance is limited to a single vCPU and thread, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core register in the poor category. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with read-only large block speeds at 30.06 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.5 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8g.medium offers a low-entry hardware profile for ARM-based development, but presents clear resource density tradeoffs. The lack of multi-threading and local storage limits its utility for intensive workloads. Database operations and web serving throughput are relatively low, as shown by weak Passmark database and poor static web serving benchmarks. This instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, software prototyping, and basic microservices that do not require high parallel processing or high-speed local I/O.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.medium is a general-purpose, ARM64-based server instance powered by a single-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 4.0 GB of memory, a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor without local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data shows average single-core CPU performance and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression, though multi-core and memory bandwidth results are poor due to the single-vCPU limitation. This instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for ARM64 architecture development but presents clear tradeoffs in parallel processing and memory throughput. It is best suited for lightweight microservices, single-threaded applications, and basic development or testing environments.
